technology.summary: Today's technology news includes the announcement of Microsoft's third-generation Maia in-house AI chip, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. Meanwhile, Amazon has over 1 million robot workers, raising questions about the future of human employees. In other news, a former Plaud executive has raised $26 million for an AI app that listens to users in the background, and the Fitbit Edge fitness tracker has been officially unveiled.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have teamed up to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. This comes as foreign portfolio investors recorded a net sale of shares worth Rs 10,148 crore, and as Indian equity benchmarks experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices. Meanwhile, a resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt. In other news, the Supreme Court of India has urged a probe into reports of patients being directed to specific pharmacies for their medications, following troubling markups on cancer drugs enforced by hospitals.

politics.summary: Today's most important politics news includes the Delhi High Court's dismissal of pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence, and the Supreme Court's decision to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar. Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a protest in Mumbai were detained, and the Delhi Police have responded to criticism over cops without name tags at the Jantar Mantar protest. In other news, former US President Donald Trump has called the US electoral process 'corrupt' in reference to an Indian election that didn't happen, and Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
